briefs.headline: Wednesday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: The platforms are quietly rewriting the numbers and the shelf heading into peak. Meta's Pixel starts counting conversions on shoppers' own devices on November 12 unless you opt out, and an audit found almost no Meta advertisers label their AI-made creative. Shopify's Catalog API now returns brands that don't sell on Shopify and lets merchants pay commission for agent-driven placements, while Riskified's survey shows shoppers want AI help but still don't trust it to buy alone.

items.title: Meta Pixel starts counting conversions on shoppers' devices from November 12, on by default
items.summary: A new Events Manager setting, "Measure conversions on customer devices," switches on for every dataset already sending events and matches some purchases on the shopper's phone or computer using details like their email. Meta hasn't said whether the recovered conversions feed bidding or carry order value, and it lands 15 days before Black Friday. Before November 12, export Meta-attributed purchases next to your real Shopify orders by day so you can tell a reporting bump from an actual lift, and keep Conversions API running.

items.title: Shopify's Catalog API can now return brands that don't sell on Shopify
items.summary: A new sources parameter on search_catalog lets agents and apps mix external brands into the same results as Shopify merchants, with data pulled from each brand's own website. External products are US-only during the beta, can't use Shopify checkout and send shoppers to the brand's product page. Shopify merchants now compete in agent results against non-Shopify brands too, so the accuracy of your titles, prices and policies matters more than the platform you're on.

items.title: Shopify's Promoted Placements beta pays agents extra commission funded by merchants' Shop Campaigns
items.summary: Merchants running Shop Campaigns with external platforms turned on now include the Catalog API, so apps and agents that surface their products earn the merchant-funded commission on top of Shopify's base rate. Buyers who click those products land in Shop. It's an early sign of paid placement inside agent shopping results, so if you run Shop Campaigns, check whether external platforms are on and watch what those sales cost you.

items.title: Riskified survey: 80% of shoppers use AI to shop, but only 11% have bought inside an AI tool
items.summary: Riskified's September survey of 5,100 consumers in five countries found 68% are likely to use AI for holiday shopping, yet just 7% are comfortable letting it buy without their approval and 43% want to approve every purchase. Some 51% say the AI platform should refund a mistaken purchase, even though Muse's and Instinct's terms put that on the user. Expect "the agent did it" disputes to land on you, so write down how you'll handle agent-placed returns and chargebacks before peak.

items.title: Audit finds 1 in 11 Meta ad files used AI media, and only 2 of 3,379 said so in the copy
items.summary: Resemble AI scanned 37,768 Facebook and Instagram ad files from 509 companies and flagged 8.9% as AI-generated or manipulated, with 70% built to look like real photos or video and 46% showing a person. The vendor used its own detector and published no error rates, but New York's synthetic performer law and EU AI Act Article 50 already put disclosure on the advertiser. If you run AI-made models or UGC-style testimonials, add a clear AI label now rather than waiting for a platform to force it.

items.title: Google Ads rolls out an AI tool that translates ad text, keywords, image text and landing pages
items.summary: The tool translates headlines, descriptions, sitelinks and keywords inside the Google Ads interface, swaps text inside images and can handle landing pages through manual URLs or a JavaScript snippet. It's still rolling out, so not every account has it yet. It makes testing a new market much cheaper, but have a native speaker review the output before you put spend behind it.

items.title: Fast Simon launches a Commerce-Native AI model that ranks products within merchant-set guardrails
items.summary: Built for Shopify brands, the model adjusts product rankings and recommendations as shoppers browse, weighing new arrivals, inventory and promotions against rules merchandisers set, such as exclusions and editorial placements. It includes a built-in A/B test against the merchant's existing merchandising. If you trial it, insist on that holdout comparison rather than vendor-reported uplift.

briefs.headline: Tuesday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: Agent shoppers arrived faster than most stores prepared for, and the platforms are now handing merchants the controls. Shopify moved its Knowledge base into every admin so you can publish what AI agents say about your store, while Forter says agentic traffic tripled in a month and The RealReal had to tighten bot defenses after an agent hoarded listings. Salesforce turned on UCP checkout on Google, and Google's AI Mode is putting Shopping ads inside answers on mobile.

items.title: Shopify builds Knowledge base into every admin, so merchants publish what AI agents say about their store
items.summary: Knowledge base now lives at Sales channels > Agentic > Knowledge base and replaces the standalone app, which goes away after January 15, 2027. Shopify drafts facts such as contact details and gift services from your published storefront pages, but nothing reaches AI agents until you publish it, and stores with more than 1,000 facts in the old app must re-add the ones they want. Open it this week, check each draft against your real shipping cutoffs, returns and holiday policies, and publish the accurate ones before peak traffic.

items.title: Forter says AI shopping agent traffic more than tripled in a month after Muse and Instinct launched
items.summary: Across Forter's merchant network, traffic from personal shopping agents more than tripled in a month, and Meta's Muse made up 46% of agentic orders in the last week of September. Orders between $50 and $200 were the most common across agents, and Forter warns that Muse crawls stores that aren't set up for agents, which is slower and more error-prone. CEO Michael Reitblat said merchants have about 6-8 weeks to react instead of the usual 6-12 months, so decide now whether you'll verify and accept agent checkouts this holiday.

items.title: The RealReal tightens bot defenses after Meta's Muse was used to hold items in carts for hours
items.summary: The Verge showed Muse could keep re-adding The RealReal listings to a cart every time the 20-minute hold expired, blocking other shoppers for hours. The RealReal's CTO said its bot defense now makes it much harder for any agent to log in, add to cart and check out, though agents can still surface listings and link to product pages. If you run cart holds, limited drops or reservations, test what an agent can do with them before shoppers' agents find the gap for you.

items.title: Salesforce B2C Commerce turns on UCP checkout in Google's Gemini and AI Mode
items.summary: Salesforce's October B2C Commerce release lets merchants switch on Universal Commerce Protocol checkout so shoppers can buy on Google surfaces like the Gemini app and AI Mode while the merchant stays merchant of record. The release also adds a Merchandising Agent that builds catalog filters from plain English, store-inventory search in Agentic Commerce Search, and a traffic report that separates chatbot-referred revenue. Agentic Commerce Search is sold as an add-on that also works for Shopify and Adobe Commerce stores.

items.title: Google's inline Shopping ads carousel in AI Mode answers now shows on mobile
items.summary: A Shopping ads carousel that had been spotted inside AI Mode responses on desktop is now appearing on mobile too, placing product ads directly in the AI-generated answer. It looks like part of a series of AI Mode ad tests rather than a formal launch. With most holiday browsing on phones, keep your Shopping feed titles, images and promotions clean, since that feed is what fills the carousel.

items.title: Fanatics launches an OpenAI-powered Shop the Look that builds in-stock outfits on product pages
items.summary: Fanatics.com and the official NFL, NBA, MLB and NHL stores now suggest coordinated game-day outfits on product pages, built by OpenAI models from enriched product, team and inventory data and refreshed daily. Fanatics' merchandising rules keep the picks compatible, and the first 50 looks were built and tested in under a day. In testing across about 30,000 MLB products the new version drove 10% higher engagement than the old Shop the Look.

items.title: Google Ads adds a Policy Summary page that sorts policy issues by cost, conversions and ROAS
items.summary: A new page at Admin > Policy > Summary groups account-level issues and ad or asset-group violations in one place. You can sort problems by cost, conversions or ROAS, so the disapprovals hurting your best campaigns surface first, and the old Policy Manager is still available. Worth a check before peak, when a disapproved Performance Max asset group can quietly cost a week of sales.

briefs.headline: Monday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: A quiet weekend, but the pattern held: the platforms keep writing more of your ad for you. Google now drops AI-written, positive-only review summaries into Search ads that advertisers can't edit, and Meta pushed its AI terms to November 20 without changing the clause that makes advertisers liable for its AI edits. Meta also put a number on over-split accounts, while Naver and Glance show agent checkout spreading beyond the US giants.

items.title: Google's AI now writes positive-only review summaries into Search ads, and advertisers can't edit them
items.summary: A new Google Ads help page describes AI-generated summaries of online reviews that appear inside Search ads in the US, UK, Australia and India, pulling positive comments from across the web. Advertisers can't edit the text, and the page gives no opt-out, reporting column or detail on which review sources are used. What third-party review sites say about your store now feeds your paid ads, so audit your reviews off your own site and fix recurring complaints before peak season.

items.title: Meta delays its new AI terms to November 20, but the advertiser liability clause hasn't changed
items.summary: Meta told Reuters on Friday that its revised Commercial and Self-Serve Ad Terms will take effect November 20 instead of October 30, after publishers complained to EU and UK regulators. Meta did not say it would change the text: the AI Features section still leaves businesses solely responsible for what Meta's AI does in their ads, and the website-crawling clause remains. Use the extra three weeks to switch off Advantage+ creative enhancements you haven't approved, and note that product browsing still turns on in existing ads October 28 unless you opt out.

items.title: Meta says ad sets under 50 weekly conversions cost about 28% more per purchase
items.summary: In a peak-season best-practice post, Meta says ad sets getting fewer than roughly 50 conversions a week ran about 28% more expensive per purchase in its own analysis, though it doesn't publish the method. Its rule of thumb is weekly budget divided by (cost per purchase x 50) equals the most ad sets your budget can support, so $20,000 a week at a $40 CPA supports about 10. Before Black Friday, consolidate thin ad sets and group your edits so campaigns aren't constantly re-entering learning.

items.title: Naver will pilot in-agent payment in its AI shopping agent, aiming to launch by year-end
items.summary: Naver said it will pilot payment inside its AI shopping agent for select product categories, so shoppers can go from search and comparison to purchase without leaving the agent, and it's bringing the agent to desktop web. Naver says the agent's monthly users and daily conversations grew about fivefold from March to August, and daily transaction volume through it quadrupled. It's another big marketplace moving checkout into the agent itself, which makes clean product data and accurate pricing the thing that wins the sale.

items.title: L Catterton invests in Glance's AI shopping platform to fund its US expansion
items.summary: Consumer investor L Catterton made a strategic investment, terms undisclosed, in Glance, the InMobi-backed AI shopping platform that runs on lock screens and connected TVs through partners like Samsung, Motorola and DIRECTV. The money backs Glance's US push, after PayPal added native checkout to its shopping agent earlier this month. Expect more shopping agents on screens you don't control, so make sure your catalog feeds and checkout options are ready to be surfaced outside your own site.

briefs.headline: Friday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: The platforms are switching AI on for you and handing you the bill. Meta's new terms make advertisers solely responsible for whatever its AI changes in their ads from October 30, and Google quietly added Performance Max options that pull images and videos from your site and social channels, with one reportedly on by default. Etsy went the other way, banning bot-made listings and requiring a real photo of every item, while Anthropic's new Claude Duet joins the agents that can buy with Shop Pay and Link.

items.title: Meta's October 30 terms make advertisers solely responsible for what its AI changes in their ads
items.summary: Meta's revised Commercial Terms add an 'AI Features' section that, per Adweek's reading, makes advertisers solely responsible for anything Meta's AI creates or edits in their ads, including features Meta switches on itself, and continued use counts as acceptance. It landed the same week advertisers like Bookshop.org reported Meta 'enhancing' their ads with imagery nobody on their team made. Before October 30, open every active campaign's creative settings, turn off the generative enhancements you haven't approved, and spot-check live ads for edits.

items.title: Google Performance Max adds Landing page images and Sourced videos, and one may already be on
items.summary: Two new asset optimization toggles let Google pull images from your website and videos from your social channels, landing pages and linked YouTube channels into Performance Max, with up to 10 sourced videos per asset group. The advertiser who spotted it says Sourced videos was enabled automatically. Check each PMax campaign's asset optimization settings now, and make sure you actually hold ad rights to any creator or UGC video on your socials before leaving it on.

items.title: Etsy bans AI-made patterns and recipes, bot-generated listings, and listings without a real photo
items.summary: Etsy will stop allowing AI-generated recipes, patterns and instructions, bars listings created by bots with no human involvement, and requires at least one unedited photo of the actual item. Etsy said buyers' confusion over AI content has become a top-three barrier to shopping more often. AI-assisted art stays allowed with disclosure, so sellers using AI for listing copy or mockups should add real product photos and clear disclosures before the rules bite.

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, an agent that can buy with Stripe Link and Shop Pay
items.summary: Claude Duet is a research-preview app for professionals and small business owners that monitors connected apps, works in the background and checks in before acting. Stripe says Duet can buy things anywhere online with Link's agent wallet using a virtual card after the user approves each purchase, and can send invoices, manage prices and issue refunds through Stripe MCP; TechCrunch reports Shop Pay checkout too. It's another big agent that buys through wallets your store may already accept, so Shop Pay and Link being on at checkout matters more each week.

items.title: The Verge finds shopping agents tripping over retailer bot checks as often as outright bans
items.summary: Testing Meta's Muse, The Verge found it caught in Target's bot check one day and let through the next, while Amazon hard-blocks it. Target told the reporter that agent access can depend on how the agent approaches the site and that some areas stay closed to protect accounts. If you want agent orders, check whether your bot protection or firewall is quietly blocking them; if you don't, write down a policy rather than leaving it to whatever your firewall happens to do.

items.title: A field guide to Google Merchant Center's six conversational attributes for AI Mode
items.summary: Search Engine Land breaks down the six optional attributes Google uses to understand products in AI Mode and AI Overviews: question_and_answer, document_link, related_product, item_group_title, variant_option and popularity_rank. Google recommends adding them through a supplemental feed so your main product data stays untouched, and they don't affect existing approvals. Start with Q&A on your top sellers, then use the AI performance insights report to see where you show up.

items.title: Therabody launches an AI shopping assistant on AWS's packaged Agentic Shopping Assistant in under 90 days
items.summary: Therabody's assistant, Jason, asks shoppers about their goal, budget and lifestyle, then recommends a device and explains why. It's built on AWS's Agentic Shopping Assistant, configured around Therabody's own products and compliance rules, and launched in under 90 days. For brands with considered purchases, a guided-selling assistant is becoming an off-the-shelf build rather than a custom project.

briefs.headline: Thursday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: Agents are getting rules of the road. Walmart opened an MCP gateway for shopping agents with its own terms, spending limits and agent-only purchase history, and Meta said it will charge businesses a fee on sales its Muse agent helps close. On the ad side, the platforms are taking more of the wheel: ChatGPT Ads will start rewriting copy and URLs by default on October 30, and a new Semrush study finds AI Overviews on 88% of tracked commercial searches.

items.title: Walmart launches an MCP Agent Gateway, Agent Profiles with spending limits, and terms shopping agents must follow
items.summary: Walmart is giving approved agents an MCP connection to shop Walmart and Sam's Club, starting as a beta for companies and developers, and next month adds Agent Profiles so shoppers can see each agent's purchases separately and cap spending at amounts like $50, $100 or $200. Its new agent terms say purchases need approval by default, agents never see card details, normal returns apply even when an agent gets it wrong, and agents that break the rules get blocked. It's the clearest template yet for what a retailer's agent policy looks like, and a useful checklist if you're deciding whether to block or welcome agents on your own store.

items.title: Meta says 10 million people have set up Muse, shopping is the top use, and businesses will pay a fee on agent sales
items.summary: On Meta's Q3 earnings call, Mark Zuckerberg said more than 10 million people in the US and Canada have set up Muse agents in about six weeks, and that shopping is the most common use, with average purchases over $200. Meta plans to keep Muse free for users and charge businesses a fee on the transactions it helps complete, though no rate or start date was given. The same call put creator partnership ads at a $15 billion run rate, up 97% year over year, so creator-led ads and agent-driven sales are both becoming line items DTC brands will pay Meta for.

items.title: ChatGPT Ads will rewrite headlines, descriptions and landing URLs by default starting October 30
items.summary: OpenAI told advertisers it will switch on creative enhancements for new and existing self-serve ChatGPT campaigns on October 30, letting the system adjust headlines and descriptions, resize images, translate copy and optimize destination URLs based on the conversation. Those variations can run without you reviewing each one. If you advertise on ChatGPT and have claims, pricing or compliance copy that can't drift, check the account and campaign toggles in Ads Manager before the date.

items.title: Semrush finds AI Overviews on 88% of tracked commercial searches, with ecommerce queries jumping the most
items.summary: Across 400 US commercial keywords tracked from September 2025 to August 2026, AI Overview coverage rose from 45.75% to 88%, and to 97% when weighted by search volume. Ecommerce queries had the biggest rise, from 32.62% to 85.11%, and ecommerce price and cost searches went from under 5% to over 71%. For product pages and buying guides, that means the AI summary is now the first impression on most decision-stage searches, so check what it says about you and which review sites it cites.

items.title: Cafe24 turns on WebMCP for every store on its platform
items.summary: South Korean commerce platform Cafe24 applied WebMCP to all stores built on it, exposing 11 shopping functions to browser agents, from product search and option selection to cart edits, single-item purchase and order lookups. Shoppers still handle login and final payment themselves. Coming a day after BigCommerce did the same, it shows platforms making agent-readable storefronts a default feature rather than a merchant project.

items.title: Meta Ads Manager appears to add product-level spend and sales for catalog campaigns
items.summary: Advertisers are reporting a new 'Top products in your campaign' panel in Ads Manager that ranks catalog items by spend, clicks, views, purchases and attributed orders, filterable by ad set. Meta hasn't documented it yet, and one advertiser says it counts sitelinks as products, so treat the numbers with care. If it's in your account, it's a quick way to spot products soaking up budget without sales before Black Friday.

items.title: Stripe Treasury for agents lets ChatGPT, Claude and other agents check balances and pay invoices with approval
items.summary: Stripe now lets businesses connect agents to their Stripe Treasury accounts through its MCP server to check balances, pay invoices, move money between accounts and convert currencies. Owners choose which accounts an agent can see, whether it can act or only read, and when money movement needs a human sign-off, with agent spending limits coming in the next few weeks. For small brands already on Stripe, it's a practical step toward agents handling back-office finance, not just storefront tasks.

briefs.headline: Wednesday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: Agent readiness is turning into a platform default instead of a project. Commerce switched on WebMCP for eligible BigCommerce stores with no merchant setup, Target finally shipped its own shopping assistant, and Yotpo launched a tool that shows brands where AI answers leave them out. On the payments side, Money20/20 kept circling trust: Amex research says shoppers are far more comfortable letting AI research than letting it buy, while Mastercard and Evervault shipped new ways to cap what an agent can spend and see.

items.title: Commerce and Cloudflare turn on WebMCP by default so browser agents can shop BigCommerce stores
items.summary: Eligible BigCommerce stores now tell a shopper's browser agent what they sell and what actions it can take, so the agent can search real products, prices and stock, fill a cart, and hand back a link to finish checkout on the merchant's site. It's on by default with no code changes, and merchants can switch it off in a new settings menu that manages all of Commerce's AI connections. If you're on BigCommerce, check that setting and your catalog data now, because agents will read exactly what's there.

items.title: Amex at Money20/20: 59% of shoppers are fine with AI research, but only 36% with AI buying
items.summary: On a day-two panel, Amex Digital Labs cited research showing 59% of US consumers are comfortable using AI for product research versus 36% for letting an agent complete a purchase, and nearly 75% say buying from a preferred merchant still matters when AI shops for them. Walmart and Google speakers echoed that agents should support the retailer relationship, with Google pointing to UCP-enabled checkouts already live with US merchants. For brands, discovery is where agents matter today, and brand loyalty still carries into agent-led purchases.

items.title: Target launches Ask Target, a beta AI shopping assistant, ahead of the holidays
items.summary: Target released a beta of its Ask Target chatbot in time for holiday shopping, catching up with Amazon, Walmart and Lowe's, which have offered assistants for months. It answers general Target questions as well as gift queries, and comes two months after Target hired former Lowe's AI head Chandhu Nair as chief AI officer. Walmart says Sparky users build baskets 40% larger, so expect shoppers to get used to asking a retailer's own bot instead of browsing.

items.title: Yotpo launches Discover to show brands where AI answers recommend competitors instead of them
items.summary: Discover tracks where a brand's products appear in AI shopping answers by product, category, region and buying stage, shows which competitors get recommended instead, and turns the gaps into content and product-page fixes using reviews and other customer signals. Yotpo's case studies report Aetrex saw a 62% increase in No. 1 placements in AI answers, and an MCP connection lets teams pull the data into Claude and similar tools. It works with Shopify, Salesforce Commerce, Adobe Commerce and BigCommerce.

items.title: Mastercard opens early access to Agent Pay for Machines, built on the x402 payment protocol
items.summary: At Cloudflare Connect, Mastercard showed agents paying for digital services with signed vouchers that stay inside a budget and task the business approves, then opened early access to its APIs and documentation after pilots with Cloudflare, Coinbase and others. The demo had a marketing agency's agent buy social research and generated campaign images on its own. It's aimed at agents buying data and tools, not shoppers buying products, but it's a preview of how spend limits for agents will work.

items.title: Evervault's Browser Tokens let agents check out on any site without seeing the real card
items.summary: Evervault swaps card numbers, passwords and personal data for short-lived tokens that agents and hosted browsers handle instead, restoring the real values only for destinations the developer approves. It works on existing checkout pages without merchants adopting any agent protocol. That means more agent orders may arrive through your normal checkout looking like ordinary browser sessions, which is another reason to know how your fraud tools treat automated traffic.

items.title: Reign and WooCommerce partner on AI-built checkouts and payment routing for social-first brands
items.summary: Reign will bring its AI-built checkout pages, routing across more than 150 payment integrations, failed-payment recovery and portable subscription billing to WooCommerce stores, with the extension expected in Q1 2027. It's pitched at direct-response and subscription brands driving traffic from TikTok, Instagram and Facebook that want to own their checkout and cards on file. Nothing ships this year, but it's one to watch if you run subscriptions on WooCommerce.

briefs.headline: Tuesday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: Money20/20 USA opened in Las Vegas, and the agent conversation has moved from checkout buttons to trust: proving who an agent works for, what it's allowed to spend, and who eats the loss when it gets it wrong. Skyfire and Forter are feeding agent identity into fraud decisions, Visa has trusted agents paying real invoices through supplier portals, and Proof and Circle showed identity and payment in one step. Meanwhile TikTok is shortening the path from video to purchase, and analysts see Walmart's open-door approach to agents paying off while Amazon keeps them out.

items.title: Forter adds Skyfire's agent identity tokens to its fraud decisions as agent orders quadruple
items.summary: Forter now uses Skyfire's Know Your Agent (KYA) tokens inside its fraud product for agent purchases, so merchants can tell an authorized shopping agent from a bot pretending to be one. The companies say agentic orders flowing through Forter's network have more than quadrupled since August, and that standard bot defenses often decline legitimate agent buyers. Merchants don't need to change their checkout, but it's worth asking your fraud vendor how it scores agent traffic before the holiday rush.

items.title: Visa, BILL and Billtrust launch a live pilot where trusted AI agents pay supplier invoices
items.summary: BILL's payment agent, registered through Visa's Trusted Agent Protocol and Agentic Directory, now pays approved invoices end to end through Billtrust supplier portals using tokenized cards and the buyer's payment rules. Visa says the agent authentication can stand in for CAPTCHA and other bot blocks without a separate agent login, and the pilot is processing live transactions. It's B2B for now, but it shows how verified agents could get past the same bot walls that block them on retail sites.

items.title: Proof and Circle demo an agent that proves who it buys for and pays in USDC in one step
items.summary: At Money20/20, Proof and Circle showed an agent presenting a verified identity credential over Proof's x401 protocol, then paying in USDC from a Circle Agent Wallet over x402. The merchant sees only the identity details it needs and gets signed proof of payment it can use in a dispute. It's a demo, not a product launch, but it points to age-restricted and high-value sellers being able to check identity and authority in the same exchange as the payment.

items.title: TikTok teams with Shoplazza to power Buy Direct and its Shopping Assistant
items.summary: Shoplazza is a commerce and payment partner for TikTok's new Buy Direct, which lets people buy from brands inside TikTok over the Universal Commerce Protocol while the brand stays merchant of record. TikTok's Shopping Assistant also answers product questions from merchant-supplied page data in the in-app browser. If you sell through TikTok ads, accurate product data and a short path to checkout now matter as much as the creative.

items.title: Bank of America analysts say Walmart's open stance on shopping agents positions it to win
items.summary: A Bank of America note published Monday cites Walmart's integrations with multiple AI ecosystems, its own Sparky assistant, and partnerships with agents like Meta's Muse as reasons it's well placed if shoppers hand buying to agents. Amazon blocks Muse and bans outside automated shopping tools. The analysts say most people still use AI to research rather than buy, so the bet is about getting in while habits form, and it leaves open what agent checkout does to retail ad businesses.

items.title: At Money20/20, identity vendors say agents are breaking merchant fraud signals
items.summary: On a Know Your Agent panel, Skyfire's CEO said a real agent can show up from IP addresses in three locations, which is exactly what merchant fraud tools treat as a red flag. VGS's CEO said properly verified agents with clear spend limits could eventually shift some liability to issuers and networks and away from merchants, who are the least prepared to absorb it. Nothing has changed in the rules yet, so for now chargeback risk on agent orders still sits with the seller.

items.title: Perfect Corp. uses generative AI to remove shoppers' own glasses during virtual try-on
items.summary: Perfect Corp. added a Glasses Removal feature to its eyewear virtual try-on that rebuilds the face behind a shopper's current glasses, so they can keep them on and still see each new frame clearly. It replaces older frame-masking methods that left smudges and outlines, and works on websites, apps and in-store kiosks through one integration. Brands only need three product photos per frame to create a try-on item.

briefs.headline: Monday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: The tools for selling through AI agents kept shipping into the weekend, but most merchants still aren't letting agents buy. Shopify now passes shopper consent choices through agent carts and checkouts, Vercel and Fabric shipped ways to make Shopify catalogs readable to agents, and BrightEdge says agent purchases are growing about 43% a month while only about 3% of the ecommerce companies it works with let agents complete a transaction. On the ad side, Google started testing ads in personalized AI Mode and Meta walked back the AI-training language in its new business terms, so check your settings and terms before the holiday push.

items.title: Agent purchases are growing 43% a month, but only about 3% of sellers let agents check out
items.summary: A Heard on the Street column cites BrightEdge estimates that purchases made through AI agents are growing about 43% month over month and have roughly quadrupled since April, while only about 3% of the ecommerce companies BrightEdge works with allow agents to complete transactions. Amazon blocks outside agents like Meta's Muse and OpenAI's Dots, Target only admits approved agents, and Walmart has partnered with OpenAI and Google. The open questions for merchants are returns and chargebacks when an agent buys the wrong thing, and how to prove an agent is authorized to pay.

items.title: Shopify's Checkout MCP and Cart MCP now carry shopper consent choices from AI agents
items.summary: Agents using Shopify's Checkout MCP and Cart MCP on UCP version 2026-08-25 can now show shoppers the store's own privacy and marketing options, including email and SMS opt-in, and pass those choices to the shop with the cart, checkout and order. If an agent sends no consent, Shopify applies the shop's default settings for the buyer's country, and defaults to opt-out when the country is unknown. That means agent-placed orders can grow your email and SMS lists, but only if your consent defaults and policy pages are set up the way you want.

items.title: Vercel Shop, an open source agent-ready Shopify storefront, is generally available
items.summary: Vercel's open source Next.js storefront template for Shopify is now generally available, built on the rebuilt Hydrogen SDK. The same product URL can serve a normal page to shoppers or machine-readable price, availability and options to agents, and the template exposes UCP catalog search and cart tools over MCP at the merchant's own domain. It's mainly relevant to headless or Plus brands weighing a rebuild, since it bundles agent access, structured data and an on-site shopping assistant in one codebase.

items.title: Fabric launches a Shopify app that enriches catalogs so AI agents can recommend products
items.summary: Fabric's new Shopify app syncs a store's full catalog, uses a merchant agent to help enrich product attributes, and publishes the results back to the theme. Enriched attributes are written to metafields, JSON-LD Product schema is added for agents, and merchants choose whether each attribute is shown to shoppers, agents or both. It's another sign that thin product data, not missing protocols, is now the main reason products don't show up in agent answers.

items.title: Google starts testing ads in AI Mode for users who connect their apps
items.summary: Google is testing ads in AI Mode for people who opt into Personal Intelligence, which was ad-free when it launched, and insights from their connected Google apps may now help pick which ads they see. Google says ads won't be targeted directly on Gmail or Photos content, advertisers can't access connected apps, and sensitive data isn't used. No new advertiser controls or targeting options have been announced, so for now the practical step is to watch AI Mode placements in your Search and Shopping reporting.

items.title: Meta removes AI-training language from its new commercial terms after pushback
items.summary: Meta's updated commercial terms had said it could use content from a business account's domains and web pages to develop and train its products, which legal experts quoted by Nieman Lab read as permission to scrape any site with a Meta business account. Meta has now removed that provision and says the consolidated crawling terms only apply to its ads and business products and don't change how it uses web crawlers. Brands advertising on Meta should still expect its crawler to read their product pages for ad and shopping features, so keep prices, availability and policies on those pages accurate.

items.title: Google Merchant Center adds a warranty attribute for all product types
items.summary: Merchant Center now accepts a warranty attribute for general products in Shopping ads and free listings, not just vehicle ads in Japan, using a duration and a unit of months or years (for example 3:year). It's optional in most cases but may be required where local rules demand warranty disclosure, such as Quebec's Bill 29. Google hasn't promised any visibility boost, but it's one more structured field shoppers and AI answers can compare, so add it where you offer a real warranty.

briefs.headline: Friday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: AI shopping is moving into the places people already spend time, and the merchant's own site is turning into a later step in the journey. Google's Universal Cart now tracks products across retailers in Search and Gemini, Meta will start opening in-app product pages from live ads on October 28 unless advertisers opt out, and PayPal is putting checkout inside Glance's preinstalled shopping agent. Stripe says agent-driven commerce took off in September, so the brands that keep their feeds clean and check their Meta defaults this month will hold more control going into Black Friday.

items.title: Google's Universal Cart goes live in US Search and the Gemini app
items.summary: Google began rolling out Universal Cart in the U.S. on October 15, letting shoppers save products from multiple retailers across AI Mode in Search and the Gemini app and get alerts on price drops and restocks from its Shopping Graph. Checkout runs on the Universal Commerce Protocol, either through Google Pay inside the cart or by handing items to the merchant's own cart, and the merchant stays the seller of record; Google names Nike, Sephora, Target, Walmart, Wayfair and many Shopify merchants. Because the cart also surfaces promo codes and card perks, accurate price, availability and promotion data in your product feed matters more heading into the holidays.

items.title: Meta will switch on product browsing in live Facebook and Instagram ads on October 28
items.summary: Meta told advertisers it will add product browsing to existing ads starting October 28 unless they opt out, so a tap may open an in-app page with product info and personalized suggestions before the shopper reaches your site. Meta cites 3% more conversions from an August test across about 117,700 advertisers but doesn't say which conversions or at what cost, and PPC Land found no public Meta documentation of the change. Decide before the 28th whether to use the opt-out or the per-ad toggle in Advantage+ Creative and Destination settings, and watch for reporting that mixes your creative's results with the experience Meta generates around it.

items.title: Stripe says agentic commerce activity started "going vertical" in September
items.summary: Stripe president John Collison said on his Cheeky Pint podcast, talking with Mark Zuckerberg and Alexandr Wang, that agent-driven commerce on Stripe took off in September, though he shared no figures. Wang said Meta's Muse is one of the first services where people fully delegate purchases, and Zuckerberg said far more businesses are asking Meta to integrate than are trying to block it. Treat it as a direction rather than a number, and check that your checkout and fraud rules can handle agent-placed orders before peak season.

items.title: PayPal brings native checkout to Glance's AI shopping agent
items.summary: Glance, an InMobi-backed AI shopping app that carriers and device makers preinstall on phones, made PayPal its only native in-app checkout on October 15. Shoppers can try on clothes with an AI avatar built from a single photo, build a cart and pay without leaving Glance, which says it is embedded on more than 60 million mobile and connected-TV devices. Merchants join through PayPal's agentic commerce services at paypal.ai, which PayPal pitches as one integration for multiple AI shopping surfaces with real-time pricing and availability.

items.title: Wix's Symphony agents can now pay suppliers and bills through Stripe's Link wallet
items.summary: Symphony by Wix, Wix's standalone multi-agent system for small businesses, now connects to Link, Stripe's digital wallet, so its agents can reorder stock, pay supplier invoices and send make-good gift cards on the owner's behalf. The owner approves each spend within a 10-minute window by WhatsApp or SMS, and Stripe pays with a token or one-time virtual card capped at the approved amount. It is rolling out to Symphony users with a U.S. Link account and shows agents starting to handle the buying side of running a store, not just the selling side.

items.title: Shopify Flow can now buy shipping labels automatically
items.summary: A new Shopify Flow action buys shipping labels as qualifying orders come in, using the carrier, service, package type, weight and ship date you choose. You can target orders by tag, by product, single-item orders, or any mix of order attributes, and orders that don't match are left alone. Starting from the ready-made template is a quick way to take label work off simple, repeatable orders before holiday volume hits.

items.title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, an open-weight model built for coding and agent work
items.summary: Meta launched Muse Spark Open on October 15, an 816-billion-parameter, natively multimodal open-weight model with a 1 million token context window that Meta says beats other popular open-weight models on its own evaluations. It is available through several API platforms and can run locally on a Mac Studio with at least 1TB of RAM. For ecommerce teams it adds another open option for catalog enrichment, support and internal agents where you want more control over data and cost.

briefs.headline: Thursday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: As AI takes over more of the ad spend and the buying, the platforms are moving the guardrails rather than removing them. Google now lets advertisers cap Display and Search partner spend by percentage, Meta is dropping manual placements on Sales campaigns in favor of account-level exclusions, and Amex wants every agent purchase tied to a token that proves what the shopper actually asked for. Control is shifting from individual settings to rules you set once, so teams that write those rules down before the holiday rush will keep the most say over where their money goes.

items.title: Google Ads lets advertisers cap Display and Search partner spend by percentage
items.summary: Google added channel prioritization and budget allocation controls to Search, Shopping, Performance Max and Demand Gen, rolling out progressively from October 15. Advertisers can mark Search partners or the Display Network as low priority and set a best-effort daily cap as a share of average daily budget, with 0% stopping spend there, though ranking alone changes nothing for campaigns that aren't budget-limited. In February 2027, Search campaigns with Display turned on migrate automatically, and Google says a low-priority 50% allocation keeps today's setup.

items.title: Amex publishes a framework to block agent purchases that don't match what the shopper asked for
items.summary: American Express released its Intent Intelligence Framework on October 13. A Create Intent API captures the shopper's instructions, such as merchant, maximum budget and product preferences, and once the shopper authenticates, a Proof of Intent Token is used to get a scoped payment credential for checkout. Amex says it can stop a purchase that strays from the request, like an agent buying Adidas when the shopper asked for white Nikes in size 9, so clear brand, title and variant data matter more for agent-placed orders.

items.title: Meta removes manual placement selection for Sales, Leads, Engagement and App campaigns
items.summary: Meta is removing ad-set-level manual placement selection for Sales, Leads, Engagement and App promotion campaigns, while Awareness and Traffic keep it. Brands can still block Audience Network, Facebook Marketplace and the right column through account-level exclusions, now settable by campaign objective, and can adjust bids with placement value rules. Ads won't deliver where their media doesn't fit, so upload several aspect ratios (up to 10 images and videos per ad); Meta cites an experiment showing 10% lower cost per result with Advantage+ placements.

items.title: Google Ads report shows which AI Max headlines and landing pages each search term got
items.summary: A new Search terms and ad combinations report is appearing in some Google Ads accounts, putting each triggering query next to the headlines, descriptions and landing page it served. It also flags whether the match came from AI Max expanded matching or URL inclusions and whether the assets were advertiser-provided. Rollout timing isn't confirmed, but where it shows up, check top-spending terms for mismatches like a basic query landing on a premium product.

items.title: Google AI Mode Shopping ads now display merchant promotions
items.summary: Shopping ads at the bottom of Google AI Mode answers are now showing offers such as "Buy 4 get $20 off," with a details popup on click, the same way promotions already appear in regular Shopping ads. Until now these AI Mode ads showed only the image, name, price, brand and reviews. With holiday offers coming, get promotions submitted and approved in Merchant Center early so they can appear on this surface too.

items.title: Shopify brings Sidekick into the checkout and customer accounts editor
items.summary: Sidekick is now available in the desktop checkout and accounts editor, where merchants can ask how to configure checkout and customer account settings, get app recommendations and search the Help Center. In the Checkout Blocks app it can explain configured blocks and payment, delivery and validation functions. It guides rather than edits, pointing to the settings or steps so the team makes the change itself.

items.title: Grok Voice 3.0 launches as a speech-to-speech model aimed at support calls
items.summary: Grok Voice 3.0 is available in the Voice Agent API at $0.08 per minute, the same price as its predecessor, with under-one-second latency and a first-place 86.9 on Artificial Analysis's Speech-to-Speech Index. The company says Starlink call centers use it for 20,000 calls a day, with about 70% resolved without a human. For teams weighing voice agents for order status, returns or phone sales, per-minute pricing makes the cost easy to compare against current support spend.

briefs.headline: Wednesday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: Shopify just opened the rails so any AI agent can search a billion products and check out with Shop Pay, without a special partnership. The same day, Shopify's own data says AI-referred sessions convert far better than organic search, Forter shipped tools to tell trusted agents from fraud bots, and Klaviyo put its marketing agent in every account. Discovery and checkout are moving into chat; the operators who win will be the ones whose catalogs, fraud rules, and retention stack are ready for agents they don't control.

items.title: Shopify opens catalog search and Shop Pay checkout to any MCP agent
items.summary: Shopify launched Shop MCP on October 13 so compatible AI agents can search more than a billion products in Shopify Catalog, build carts, and complete Shop Pay checkout through one MCP connection at mcp.shop.com, without a bilateral partnership like the earlier Meta Muse deal. Shoppers connect an agent to their Shop account, set rules such as budget caps or fast shipping only, and must approve each purchase; orders land in the merchant's Shopify admin like any other order. The developer changelog lists 17 tools covering search, Shop sign-in, carts, checkout, and order tracking, and says search needs no API key.

items.title: Shopify data: AI-referred sessions convert 80% higher than organic search
items.summary: Shopify's Entrepreneur Effect research hub reports that between April and June 2026, AI-referred sessions converted 80% higher than organic search traffic, and orders from those referrals had a 14% higher average order value. The same report says businesses on Shopify generated more than $1.2tn in economic activity worldwide over the past year. Treat the lift as platform-reported, not an independent A/B test, but it is a clear signal to treat AI discovery the way you treat SEO and paid search: with feed quality, compare-at accuracy, and agent-ready product data.

items.title: Forter launches Agentic Commerce Engine to ID trusted AI shoppers and run headless checkout
items.summary: Forter said on October 13 that Agentic Commerce Engine is live: Fraud Management for Agentic Commerce to spot legitimate assistants versus abuse bots, Agentic Orchestration for headless checkout via agentic protocols through a single no-code integration, and an AI Activity Dashboard showing which agents are on the site. Forter claims agentic orders on its network are up fourfold since August and automated fraud doubled in 60 days; those are company figures. Merchants still running bot-block-everything rules should audit whether they are also killing real agent-driven orders ahead of peak.

items.title: Klaviyo makes Composer generally available with scheduled tasks, citations, and SQL
items.summary: Klaviyo's Composer marketing agent is now available to every Klaviyo customer. It answers performance questions with visible citations and industry benchmarks across more than 205,000 customers, runs recurring audits on a schedule in the cloud, and can apply team-defined Skills. The same release wave adds SQL in Klaviyo Data Platform so Composer can answer questions outside pre-built skills, plus Social Performance revenue reporting for Instagram actions and multi-market Customer Agent support for Shopify Markets.

items.title: Spangle launches Halo, a retailer-side agent for UCP and MCP shopping conversations
items.summary: Spangle AI announced Spangle Halo on October 13, an AI merchant agent meant to represent retailers inside agent-to-agent shopping through Universal Commerce Protocol, Model Context Protocol, and browser-based flows. It uses Spangle's brand-specific demand and business intelligence to choose what to merchandise and how to grow basket value within retailer-set rules. Availability starts with select enterprise retailers; Spangle cites prior results at REVOLVE (60% ROAS lift, 50% revenue-per-visit, 30% conversion) that are vendor-reported and refer to existing products, not Halo specifically.

items.title: Google makes Gemini 4 Argon broadly available at intro API pricing
items.summary: Google opened Gemini 4 Argon globally on October 13 for developers and enterprises via the Gemini API, and for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search, and Google Antigravity. Introductory API pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30, then $4/$20. Argon targets long multi-step coding, agentic, and domain work with a 1M unified token limit; ecommerce teams building internal agents or catalog tooling should note the intro window before rates double.

briefs.headline: Tuesday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: Getting named by AI and getting chosen by AI are turning out to be different jobs. Semrush's new index finds fewer than half of the brands AI tools mention are also the sources those tools cite, and the New York Times reports brands paying startups to rewrite their catalogs for agents. Platforms are handing merchants more of the controls at the same time: Microsoft lets advertisers steer AI-written ad copy, Salesforce made catalog-trained agent search standard, and Google turned product image quality from a gate into a ranking factor.

items.title: Semrush finds most brands AI names are not the sources it cites
items.summary: Semrush's second 2026 AI Visibility Index, covering January to July across ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Mode and AI Overviews, finds that fewer than half of the top 100 brands each tool names also appear among its top 100 cited sources. Tesco and Asda are named at similar rates, but in July Tesco was ChatGPT's 25th most-cited UK domain and Asda was 606th. Semrush is owned by Adobe and says the study does not link visibility to sales, so use it as a prompt to check whether your own pages are being used as sources, not just whether your brand gets named.

items.title: Brands are paying startups to make their catalogs readable to AI shopping agents
items.source: The New York Times (via The Seattle Times)
items.summary: A New York Times report profiles startups such as Limy, Gauge and New Generation that sell AI-visibility work to brands. Online cabinet retailer RTA Store paid New Generation $15,000 to restructure its site and product content for agents, and its CEO expects to eventually spend up to $12,000 a month on it. One AI marketing founder warns the models change faster than anyone can game them, which argues for fixing product facts and structured data before paying for tricks.

items.title: Salesforce makes catalog-trained Agentic Commerce Search standard for Shopper Agent
items.summary: Salesforce's Winter '27 release became generally available on October 12, and Agentic Commerce Search is now standard for all Shopper Agent customers. It trains a small language model on each merchant's catalog and shopper behavior to handle natural-language queries instead of exact keyword matches. Salesforce reports a 13% conversion lift and 17% higher add-to-cart rates in early results, company figures with no method published.

items.title: Google stops blocking products with low-quality images from Shopping ads and free listings
items.summary: Google updated its Merchant Center help page to say products flagged for blurry, pixelated or low-resolution images will keep showing in ads and free listings; the old wording said they could be held back until the images improved. That turns image quality from an eligibility gate into a performance problem, so weak images now cost clicks quietly instead of triggering a disapproval you would notice. Google also recently raised the minimum product image size in Merchant Center to 500x500 pixels.

items.title: Microsoft lets advertisers tell AI Max what to say and avoid in generated ads
items.summary: Microsoft Advertising added messaging guidelines to the text guardrails for AI Max campaigns, so advertisers can name themes, claims, products, offers or topics to emphasize or avoid in auto-generated assets. Guardrails now allow up to 25 term exclusions and up to 40 messaging guidelines, and the guidelines are in a closed pilot for now. Brands that sell on specific claims, like shipping terms or materials, should write that list before the pilot opens.

items.title: Regional grocer Strack & Van Til launches an AI concierge that clips coupons and builds lists
items.summary: Strack & Van Til, a Hy-Vee company with more than 20 stores in northwest Indiana, launched Ernie, Homesome's white-label AI Concierge, in its app and website. It connects catalog, pricing, weekly ad, coupons, loyalty and order status, so shoppers can ask for aisle deals, check points, or upload a recipe photo and get a shoppable list. Homesome pitches it as an agent regional retailers own rather than ceding shoppers to marketplaces, and says more partners get it in the coming weeks.

items.title: KakaoTalk's new assistant can reorder last week's purchase from chat history
items.summary: Kakao unveiled Kanana Space, an assistant inside KakaoTalk, which has about 50 million users, that can send messages, manage schedules and buy products with user approval. In a demo it found a user's usual bottled water from their chats, applied coupons and prepared the order up to payment, which works because Kakao runs its own commerce and wallet services. A closed beta starts in December, and it is an early look at messaging apps becoming the place repeat purchases happen.

briefs.headline: Monday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: AI shopping agents are getting written rules, and those rules decide which brands get seen, compared and paid. A file reportedly pulled from Meta's Muse tells the agent to put well-known merchants first. Shopify now passes markdowns to AI agents, and THG put Criteo sponsored products inside a shopping chat. The agent's answer is turning into a shelf with its own ranking logic, ad inventory and data needs, and Shopify is also moving store admin into Gemini and Grok.

items.title: Meta's Muse agent is told to rank well-known merchants first
items.summary: An instruction file that research firm Profound says it pulled from Muse calls it "imperative" that the top five picks come from well-known merchants. It also tells Muse to drop listings priced outside a category's normal range and to check at most three open-web stores, returning at most ten products. In-chat checkout is reserved for Meta catalog items flagged for agentic checkout, and Meta has not commented on the file.

items.title: Shopify now shares compare-at prices with AI shopping agents
items.summary: Shopify Catalog now passes compare-at prices to AI shopping agents, so a markdown shows up as a markdown in chat instead of only the current price. Merchants control it with a toggle in the Compare-at section of catalog mapping in admin. Stores that use compare-at as a fake MSRP should audit those values before agents show them as discounts.

items.title: THG Commerce puts Criteo sponsored products inside its AI shopping assistant
items.summary: THG built its AI Shopping Assistant on Google's Gemini Enterprise and now shows labeled Criteo sponsored products next to organic picks inside the conversation. THG calls it Europe's first and says early sponsored placements got more than 5x average click-through and more than 2x average conversion, company figures with no method published. The assistant also ships as SaaS that can plug into other commerce platforms.

items.title: Shopify connects store admin to Gemini, with a matching Grok connector
items.summary: Merchants can link a store they own to Gemini to create and edit products, set inventory, build collections, create percentage-off codes and run ShopifyQL analytics in chat. Orders and customers stay read-only, and refunds, cancellations, payment settings and live-theme publishing stay blocked even with write access. A near-identical Grok connector is also live in Help Center.

items.title: Google Ads starts pulling coupons from advertiser sites into ads
items.summary: Starting October 12, Google automatically extracts discount offers from advertiser sites and attaches them as promotion assets on Search and Performance Max campaigns that have location assets and no manual promotions. It is opt-out at the account level under Automated assets. Old sale banners left up on a site could appear in ads, mainly for brands with physical locations.

items.title: Amazon will sell ads that ask recent buyers for reviews, run through Ads Agent
items.summary: Review Requests invites verified recent buyers to rate or review a product. It opens in U.S. open beta in late October for listings under 1,000 ratings and reviews, and campaigns run only through Amazon Ads Agent or the Unified API. Amazon claims 3x weekly ratings and reviews from a 19-day closed beta; pricing is not published.

briefs.headline: Friday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: Agentic checkout kept spreading beyond the big platforms on Thursday. Newegg went live with UCP checkout inside Google AI Mode and Gemini, Crossmint shipped a single API for agents to pay at any online store, and Google turned Gemini into a task-running agent with Shopify and PayPal as early testers. Retailers like HP and Bunnings are also rebuilding their own sites around conversation instead of navigation.

items.title: Newegg goes live with UCP checkout in Google AI Mode and Gemini
items.summary: U.S. shoppers can now buy eligible Newegg products inside AI Mode in Google Search and the Gemini app without leaving the conversation, using Universal Commerce Protocol checkout. Newegg stays merchant of record and handles fulfillment and support. It's a template for mid-market retailers: one catalog feeding ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google checkout surfaces at once.

items.title: Crossmint launches a single API for AI agents to pay and check out
items.summary: Crossmint's Agent Commerce Toolkit combines card storage, Visa Intelligent Commerce and Mastercard Agent Pay credentials, and merchant checkout in one self-serve integration, with an open-source reference app. It lowers the bar for anyone building a shopping agent, which means more agent-driven checkouts hitting regular storefronts. Merchants should watch how bot-detection and fraud rules treat these sessions.

items.title: Google turns Gemini into a task-running agent for businesses, with Shopify and PayPal testing
items.summary: Google announced a unified Gemini agent that can carry out tasks across connected systems like Workspace, Slack, Jira and Snowflake, launching to businesses before consumers. Shopify, PayPal and On were early testers, and Google added spend caps and smart model routing to control costs. For commerce teams this is a sign that back-office agents for reporting and ops are moving into mainstream tools.

items.title: TikTok automates search ads with Smart+ and expands GMV Max and its ad network
items.summary: TikTok added a Smart+ Search Ads Campaign that automates keywords and creative, Smart+ Creative Selection for one creative approval workflow, and an expanded GMV Max that shifts spend toward TikTok Shop content that's performing. It also opened the TikTok Ad Network to U.S. advertisers across nearly 400,000 apps. Sellers should expect less manual control and more need for a steady supply of creative.

items.title: HP pilots an agentic site that rebuilds pages around what the shopper says
items.summary: HP Experience AI, in beta with a limited group of U.S. customers, lets shoppers speak or type what they need and changes what appears on HP.com, pulling in products, comparisons and follow-up questions. It's a step past the chat widget: conversation becomes the navigation. Brands with complex catalogs should watch whether this beats filters and category pages.

items.title: Bunnings brings its Buddy AI shopping agent to New Zealand
items.summary: Bunnings launched Buddy, built with Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise, on its New Zealand website and app to help customers plan projects, find products and get advice. The Australian version had to apologize in December 2025 after it gave unlicensed electrical advice. It's a reminder that shopping agents in regulated or safety categories need hard guardrails.

briefs.headline: Thursday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: Agentic checkout is moving from announcements into onboarding queues. Google started rolling out a UCP integration hub inside Merchant Center, and Sierra, Meta, Shopify, Stripe and Walmart proposed a standard for how personal agents sign in and act at stores. On the storefront side, Gap, The RealReal and Very are swapping keyword search and static pages for conversational discovery and intent-based offers.

items.title: Google starts onboarding merchants to AI Mode checkout from Merchant Center
items.summary: Google is gradually rolling out a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) integration hub in Merchant Center for U.S. merchants, with Australia and Canada to follow next year. Integrating lets merchants show a checkout button on eligible product listings in AI Mode in Google Search and in Gemini, with capabilities like cart transfer to the merchant's site. Teams already running Google Shopping should check eligibility now and scope the UCP work, because access depends on finishing that integration.

items.title: Meta, Sierra, Shopify, Stripe and Walmart propose rules for how personal agents shop
items.summary: Sierra and Meta announced the Personal Agent Protocol, an open standard for how consumers' AI agents authenticate, get permission and act with businesses through websites, APIs or company agents. Shopify, Stripe and Walmart are among the partners, and a v0.1 specification is due later this month. It arrives as some retailers block shopping agents outright, so brands should check whether their bot protection is turning away agents acting for real customers.

items.title: Gap brings conversational discovery to Old Navy and Banana Republic
items.summary: Gap Inc. unveiled natural-language product discovery for Old Navy and Banana Republic, letting shoppers describe what they want instead of translating it into keywords and filters. It is also putting Gap-brand products into AI outfit recommendations on the third-party styling app Alta Daily. When a top-20 online retailer treats the search box as replaceable, shopper expectations for every apparel site start to move.

items.title: The RealReal rolls out its Ask TRR shopping agent to all members
items.summary: After a pilot, The RealReal is launching Ask TRR, a natural-language shopping agent built with Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise, to its 45 million members. It is designed for a catalog where every item is one of one, so shoppers can search by look, era or occasion rather than exact designer names. Any brand with a large or fast-turning catalog has the same problem: keyword search buries products shoppers can't name.

items.title: Very reports a revenue lift from agentic, intent-based personalization
items.summary: UK retailer The Very Group is using Made With Intent's decision engine, which reads more than 800 behavioral signals, to decide which offers and prompts each shopper sees, including one-off discounts and personalized payment options. Very said revenue per customer rose by a fifth in one strategy during the first month, with an unquantified conversion lift. The numbers are early and company-reported, but they show onsite promotion logic shifting from fixed rules to real-time intent.

briefs.headline: Wednesday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: AI commerce is getting more native to the tools ecommerce teams already use. Shopify is putting its AI agent directly into store design, TikTok is building shopping agents and in-app checkout, and Amazon is turning ad management into an agentic workflow. The pattern is shifting from AI as a feature to AI as an operating layer across merchandising, acquisition and conversion.

items.title: Shopify puts Sidekick directly into store design
items.summary: Shopify launched Canvas, a visual design surface where merchants work with Sidekick to build and modify store layouts. Sidekick can make changes through chat while Canvas validates and reviews the resulting design, bringing an AI agent into the actual storefront-building workflow.

items.title: TikTok moves from social discovery toward agentic commerce
items.summary: TikTok is developing agentic shopping experiences around Buy Direct and Shopping Assistant. Buy Direct supports in-app checkout, while Shopping Assistant provides conversational product guidance around details, sizing, availability and purchasing. The move makes TikTok both a discovery and transaction surface.

items.title: Amazon turns campaign management into an AI agent workflow
items.summary: Amazon Ads introduced Ads Agent, bringing sponsored ads, full-funnel campaigns, display, video and audio into one agentic workflow. Advertisers can use the platform for analysis and recommendations, take actions themselves, or let Amazon's AI optimize campaigns on their behalf.

briefs.headline: Friday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: AI commerce is moving from discovery into the mechanics of the transaction. Shopify is opening checkout to browser-based agents, Salesforce is adding agentic merchandising and shopper-agent capabilities, and retailers are still split over how much access to give autonomous shoppers. For ecommerce teams, the immediate work is less about launching another chatbot and more about making catalogs, checkout and customer controls ready for agents.

items.title: Shopify opens checkout to browser-based AI agents
items.summary: Shopify has extended WebMCP support through checkout, including Shop Pay, allowing eligible browser-based AI agents to inspect and update checkout and complete a purchase after buyer authorization. The move takes agent access beyond product discovery and cart building into the actual transaction flow.

items.title: Salesforce adds agentic categorization and product comparisons to Commerce Cloud
items.summary: Salesforce's September B2C Commerce release adds agentically generated category recommendations, product comparisons inside its shopper agent, and MCP/agent plugins for commerce operations. The release pushes AI into both merchandising workflows and the shopper experience.

items.title: Retailers are splitting over how much access AI agents should get
items.summary: Retailers are taking different approaches to autonomous shopping agents: some are partnering with Meta's Muse and other AI channels, while others restrict agents because of concerns around customer data, fraud and control of the shopping experience. The operator issue is becoming an access-policy decision, not simply a technology decision.

briefs.headline: Weekly Wrap-Up: AI is moving into the commerce stack
briefs.lead: This week, the AI-commerce story became more concrete. Salesforce reported a 200% year-over-year increase in agentic search as a first step in shopping; BigCommerce introduced AI-ready catalog enrichment; Shopify moved browser-based agents into checkout; and Salesforce added more agentic merchandising and operations tooling. At the same time, retailers are making different calls on whether third-party agents should be allowed to access their stores. The practical takeaway for ecommerce teams is that AI readiness now spans the catalog, discovery layer, checkout, permissions and measurement—not just the front-end experience.

items.title: Weekly Wrap-Up: AI is moving into the commerce stack
items.summary: This week's signals connected agentic discovery, catalog enrichment, browser-based checkout, agentic merchandising and retailer access policies. The work is shifting from experimenting with AI experiences to preparing core commerce infrastructure for AI-originated shopping journeys.

briefs.headline: Wednesday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: AI is moving earlier in the ecommerce journey. Salesforce's latest commerce data shows agentic search becoming a much larger entry point for shopping, while Commerce is putting AI-ready catalog enrichment directly into BigCommerce and Feedonomics. Shopify is also adding web-native tooling for AI-driven checkout. For ecommerce teams, the common thread is clear: product data, discovery and the technical storefront are becoming part of the AI channel itself.

items.title: Salesforce says agentic search is becoming the first step in the purchase journey
items.summary: Salesforce's new State of Commerce report says agentic search grew 200% year over year as a first step in shopping. Its analysis of more than 1.5 billion global shoppers also found AI-chat referrals growing 150% to 428% year over year across the measured quarters, reinforcing the shift of product discovery away from traditional search and brand-owned properties.

items.title: BigCommerce adds AI-ready catalog enrichment inside the commerce platform
items.summary: Commerce introduced BigCommerce Catalog Enrichment and Feedonomics Enrichment to turn product catalogs into richer, structured data for AI discovery. BigCommerce merchants can generate titles, descriptions, feature bullets, FAQs, SEO metadata and structured fields directly in the control panel, with review and bulk-apply workflows.

items.title: Shopify adds WebMCP support for checkout
items.summary: Shopify's September platform changelog lists WebMCP support for checkout, alongside other infrastructure changes aimed at making storefront capabilities easier for AI and agent tooling to interact with. For merchants and developers, the signal is that agent-facing access is moving deeper into the checkout layer, not stopping at product discovery.

briefs.headline: Monday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: The AI-commerce story is getting more operational. Shopify is now tying product attributes directly to analytics, while its agentic storefronts are making AI channels a managed part of the sales stack. OpenAI is also publishing the concrete feed, checkout and payment requirements behind commerce in ChatGPT. The work for ecommerce teams is shifting from 'should we care about AI traffic?' to making the underlying catalog, measurement and transaction systems AI-ready.

items.title: Shopify connects product attributes directly to Analytics
items.summary: Shopify now lets merchants group and filter Analytics reports using metaobject fields referenced by product, variant, customer and order metafields. Category metafields such as color, material and fit are also available in Analytics, making structured catalog data more useful for merchandising and performance analysis.

items.title: Shopify treats ChatGPT as a product-discovery sales channel
items.summary: Shopify's current documentation says the ChatGPT channel is active by default for eligible stores and sends shoppers to the merchant's own checkout. Merchants can manage ChatGPT catalog access in the Agentic sales-channel settings, while product eligibility and required store policies become part of AI-channel readiness.

items.title: OpenAI's commerce protocol makes AI readiness an integration job
items.summary: OpenAI's current Agentic Commerce Protocol documentation defines the merchant-side requirements for shopping in ChatGPT: a structured product feed, checkout endpoints and delegated-payment handling. Merchants still own inventory, fulfillment, tax, risk and order acceptance, so AI commerce increasingly depends on the quality of the systems behind the storefront.

briefs.headline: Friday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: This week, agentic commerce moved further from demo territory into the plumbing of real ecommerce. Shopify is making AI channels a normal sales surface, OpenAI is defining the product-feed, checkout and delegated-payment pieces behind shopping in ChatGPT, and payments players are focusing on authorization, merchant control and accountability. The operator takeaway is straightforward: AI commerce is becoming a channel you have to build for, not just a source of referral traffic.

items.title: The next agentic-commerce bottleneck is infrastructure, not the agent
items.summary: A Mastercard discussion highlighted the infrastructure now surrounding agentic transactions: permissions, responsibility, merchant and payment-network connectivity, and safe machine-initiated purchases. Mastercard expects early mainstream use to center on low-value, high-frequency transactions where convenience matters most.

items.title: OpenAI lays out the plumbing behind shopping inside ChatGPT
items.summary: OpenAI's Agentic Commerce Protocol documentation spells out three merchant-side requirements: a structured product feed, checkout endpoints and delegated-payment handling. Merchants remain responsible for inventory, fulfillment, tax, risk and order acceptance while ChatGPT provides the shopper-facing experience.

items.title: Merchants are pushing for a seat at the agentic-commerce table
items.summary: The Merchant Advisory Group says its Agentic Commerce Working Group is developing a merchant perspective on governance, standards and economics as agents take on product research, payment selection and transaction execution. The signal is that merchants are starting to shape the rules rather than simply adapt to them.

briefs.headline: Weekly Wrap-Up: AI commerce is becoming infrastructure
briefs.lead: The biggest shift this week was the move from AI shopping as a discovery experience to AI shopping as an operating channel. Shopify is exposing merchant catalogs through multiple AI surfaces and connecting Meta's Muse to Shop Pay; OpenAI is defining the product-feed, checkout and delegated-payment mechanics for commerce inside ChatGPT; and Mastercard, banks and merchant groups are pushing on authorization, trust and merchant control. For ecommerce teams, the work is increasingly concrete: clean up product data, understand where AI traffic and sales are coming from, decide which agents get access, and make sure checkout, payment and customer-service systems can handle agent-originated orders.

items.title: Weekly Wrap-Up: AI commerce is becoming infrastructure
items.summary: This week's developments connected the full AI commerce stack: discovery and catalog exposure through Shopify's agentic storefronts; Meta Muse and Shop Pay moving discovery into checkout; OpenAI defining feeds, checkout and delegated payments for ChatGPT; and Mastercard, banks and merchant groups focusing on authorization, governance and responsibility. The practical operator agenda is to treat AI as a new commerce channel with its own catalog quality, attribution, access controls, checkout and post-purchase requirements.

briefs.headline: Thursday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: The agentic-commerce conversation is shifting from whether AI can shop to what happens when an agent actually buys. Merchants want the traffic, but today's discussion is increasingly about who owns the customer relationship, how agent actions are authorized, and who carries responsibility when something goes wrong.

items.title: Merchants want AI shoppers without giving up the customer relationship
items.summary: Mastercard says consumers are already using AI agents for shopping, but many journeys still stop at recommendations. The next hurdle is moving from recommendations to transactions while preserving merchant control, customer relationships and clear responsibility when an agent acts.

items.title: Shopify makes agentic storefronts a standard sales channel
items.summary: Shopify's current documentation shows agentic storefronts active by default for eligible stores, exposing products to AI channels including ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, Gemini, Copilot and Meta. Merchants can manage participating AI channels and see search and sales performance.

items.title: ChatGPT Ads add a measurable paid acquisition channel
items.summary: OpenAI's current advertising documentation describes impression and click buying, conversion measurement and reporting for ChatGPT Ads. For ecommerce teams, this creates a new paid channel where discovery, comparison and purchase intent happen inside a conversational interface.

briefs.headline: Wednesday Signal Brief
briefs.lead: AI commerce is starting to split into two layers: the interfaces where shoppers discover products and the infrastructure that actually completes the transaction. Shopify is leaning into the first wave with Meta's Muse and Shop Pay, while OpenAI is turning ChatGPT into a more direct advertising channel. At the same time, payment providers and banks are pushing harder on consent, fraud and control as agents move from recommendations to real transactions.

items.title: Shopify connects Meta's Muse to Shop Pay checkout
